title: Wamoduck motor bus IDs
scope: Hardware and interface information only. Nothing here is a statement about whether any policy stands or walks, in simulation or on the physical robot.

bus_topology.connector_carries: power and CAN-FD on the same XT30(2+2) connector
bus_topology.id_scope: One shared ID space. The three buses do not each number their motors 1-5: every bus uses its own five IDs out of the global range 1-15, so the IDs on a single bus are not consecutive. The left-leg bus carries 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; the right-leg bus carries 2, 4, 6, 8, 10; the neck-and-head bus carries 11, 12, 13, 14, 15.
bus_topology.id_assignment_source: Stated by the maintainer on 2026-09-16. It agrees with the maintainer's source table List_MotorID_CANFD.xlsx, sheet Sheet1, whose 15 rows split 5 / 5 / 5 across the three buses.
unverified_on_hardware: ID assignment as actually programmed into the servos

policy_action_vector.order: joint-tree order: left leg 5, right leg 5, neck/head 4
policy_action_vector.bus_id_by_action_index_note: action[0] = left hip yaw -> bus ID 1, action[1] = left hip roll -> bus ID 3, action[2] = left hip pitch -> bus ID 5, action[3] = left knee -> bus ID 7, action[4] = left ankle -> bus ID 9, action[5] = right hip yaw -> bus ID 2, and so on; action[10] to action[13] = neck pitch, head pitch, head yaw, head roll -> bus IDs 11, 12, 13, 14.
policy_action_vector.unverified_reason: The permutation above has not been checked on a physical robot. An internal deployment-contract file interprets the action vector in actuator order instead, and this repository's ROS 2 module ros2/wamoduck_ros2/wamoduck_ros2/model_contract.py does the same. The disagreement is unresolved. Do not energise the servos on the strength of this file.

bus_ids_and_names.note: Maintainer-supplied workbook. The workbook and the position deck are not redistributed in this repository; only the derived table and an exported PNG are.

bus_topology.note: Three CAN-FD segments out of the AT32 main control board, on XT30(2+2) connectors carrying power and CAN-FD; one for the left leg, one for the right leg, one for the neck and head.

joint_names.note: Every joint name in this file was checked against the URDF one by one.

actuator_names.note: The same 14 actuator names appear in models/wmduck/mjcf/robot_groundcontact.xml.

position_drawing.note: The slide was exported to PNG with Microsoft PowerPoint; the two CAD renders embedded in the deck do not carry the ID callouts, so the export is the only faithful form of the annotation.

corrections.reason: The source table has a typographical error. The URDF and the MJCF both spell the joint right_hip_yaw.

motors.note: Source table spells this joint Rightt_hip_yaw; the URDF and this file use right_hip_yaw
Not in the policy action vector: the published policies drive 14 joints and have no mouth axis. The ID is reserved for interaction features; see docs/roadmap.md
motors.reserved_for: Interaction features, planned and not implemented: sound feedback (open and close the beak in response to a human voice, with a speech-recognition module to be added later) and holding a small ball in the cavity of the mouth with the binocular structured-light depth camera. See docs/roadmap.md.
